comment: The guy is really knowledgeable, and you learn a lot from the 2 papers, despite how tough they are. He's a bad communicator, you go into tests guessing the stuff that you will be tested on. Unwelcoming in office hours. He probably wants to prep us for the world by being like a tough boss but this guy isn't a good professor. He's funny in class

This class is challenging but far from impossible. You will have to put in the work for the midterm and the papers, like all the other comments say they're tough. Major takeaway from this class is you will be SO knowledgeable about markets. Also, Earl is one of the best connections to have in the Bschool if you want a job in finance after grad.
Impeccable Boomer energy. He could actually teach a bit. Group paper and the individual company paper are insane, but I did learn quite a bit from them. Listen in class, things are clearer.

Most of the students in this class are in SMIF. Earl is VERY knowledgeable about all things finance, but his teaching style is talking and writing short notes on the board so it's up to you to write better notes. Midterm is tough and math-heavy, two papers are killer(150 pages combined, respectively),class is really tough but you will learn a lot.

Looking back, he acted as if thought he was god himself. Yet, he must have lost his passion for teaching years ago. He is great at one thing, taking a concise, interesting, and challenging subject and turning in into an unclear mess of scribbles and WSJ articles. If you are concentrating in finance and actually enjoy learning: Avoid Earl.

Imagine you are standing at the gates of hell and then the doors start to open: Welcome to portfolio 467. Ive never put in so much time & effort into one class and then not get an A. I will quite literally never forget this class due to the emotional trauma it caused me. Rip if you are taking this class -- Im sending you thoughts & prayers xoxo

John Earl geeks honestly. Yeah he rambles about the WSJ during class and talks about current events. But he's just old its kinda funny, don't pay attention if you don't want to. Tests are tough and 2 projects at the end of the year are massive. That being said, those projects are helpful if you want to go into finance.

Worst professor Ive ever had. Poor communicator. Assigns two massive papers at the end (150 pages total, no joke). Doesnt respect his students when they ask questions. Skips over material and puts it on tests. No practice problems or help whatsoever. Only take this class if you have had a banking internship beforehand.

Avoid taking Dr. Earl at all costs. He is not a good teacher. Each class seems to have no learning objectives, Earl simply reads from the WSJ and rambles about his thoughts. He turns his back to the class to write on the board in the middle of sentences which makes lessons even harder to follow. Assigns far too much work and is a poor communicator.

He doesn't really teach you anything. He just rambles about the WSJ the whole class and then gives you a huge project that everyone in the class pulled an all nighter for. He has a ton of respect from alumni, so he can help you get a job. But he doesn't really care about teaching anymore at this age.

Will make you work extremely hard for your grade. Automatic C option available. Listen to what he says in class and expectations will be more clear. He's hard on students because there's heavy competition jobs at Ivy league schools. Do well in his class and Wall Street alums will recognize your effort, and some will even ask him about you.

Earl is  hard.  He is a great guy and very funny in class to be around but you likely will not do well in there.  Top students get B's with only one A given.  It is a fun class but do not take it unless you need to do so as you will not do super well.  That being said, Earl is a smart and nice guy.

Finest course I have taken.Was crystal clear on DG Finance strategies.Leaped into Wall Street volatility with a slam dunk.Uses Socratic Teaching Method.     Seeks excellence from students.Simplifies known concepts.Erudite but understanding.There are no flying bottles in his class and he will not tip the boat.He is concise and interesting.

One of the worst. Talented profs have the ability to make complicated ideas lucid; this guys does the exact opposite. He makes the most basic concepts complicated. He was actually a distraction...I got more value from just reading the text. Has issues with the fact that he attended a 3rd tier public school, while his smart friends went Ivy.

The most comprehensive, broad yet interesting business classes.  Students compete for grades with only one A each semester. Automatic C option but still have to write huge reports. Knows all alumni on Wall Street.  Was teaching before I was born (I'm a senior). Likes image of being really mean but is pretty understanding.  Missing for interviews =o
